extracted.intended_audience: NCATS Advisory Council members, NCATS program and grants staff, and other NIH extramural staff involved in second-level (Council) review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Operating procedures for the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) Advisory Council's second-level review of grant applications, including voting processes, special-review triggers, delegated authorities, expedited/early concurrence processes, and subcommittee/exception rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written annual operating procedures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Council is required to establish general operating procedures for the review of grant applications. These procedures must be in writing and should be reviewed once a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should be documented and reviewed annually to ensure consistent application across extramural divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review: adequacy-of-review check and concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a Council meeting, Council members review an electronic summary of the peer review results for grant applications assigned to NCATS for funding consideration and consider the adequacy of the review; members are asked to concur with the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council may not change initial peer review outcomes (numeric overall impact scores, criterion scores, or designation as competitive but not discussed). Majority concurrence is the typical action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting modes: en bloc or individual actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Council may vote in either en bloc or individual actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most concurrence voting occurs through en bloc actions; individual discussion may be requested for applications removed from en bloc lists or for special issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: En bloc voting eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: En bloc voting occurs for applications that: have an overall impact score, are deemed competitive but not discussed or otherwise fall within the fundable range for a specific group of applications; are neither from a foreign institution nor include a foreign collaboration; have no unresolved human subject, animal or biohazard concern identified by the study section or NCATS staff; have no unresolved issues regarding recruitment of women, minorities, or children or data monitoring; and have no unresolved appeal letters or other issues requiring attention of the full Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Secretary determines which applications meet these criteria for en bloc; en bloc lists are shared with Council members in advance for review and removal requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (human subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about protection of human subjects (Code 48) require specific Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are not eligible for simple en bloc concurrence and must be discussed by Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (inclusion of women and minorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications a Division/Office plans to award with an unresolved inclusion issue ("U" code) related to inclusion of women and minorities require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable inclusion policy references and implementation guidance should be consulted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (inclusion across the lifespan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications a Division/Office plans to award with an unresolved inclusion issue ("U" code) related to Inclusion Across the Lifespan require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council must review unresolved inclusion-across-lifespan concerns prior to award recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (use of animals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about protection of animals in research (Code 44) require specific Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal welfare protections and OLAW/PHS policy references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (biohazards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about biohazards require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biohazard concerns identified by study section or NCATS staff preclude en bloc concurrence until resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (select agents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about use of select agents require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select agent compliance must be addressed before funding recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (authentication of key resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about authentication plans for key biological and/or chemical resources require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentication plans should be adequate to address reproducibility and resource validity concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (resource sharing plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about resource sharing plans require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource sharing expectations tied to NIH policy should be satisfied before concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (training in responsible conduct of research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposed for award with unresolved concerns about plans for training in the responsible conduct of research require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must align with NIH expectations for RCR training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues requiring specific Council consideration (discretionary presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications program staff present to Council for items such as adding substantial funds or years when obtaining Council's advice for public health, political, or scientific reasons is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These discretionary items may be brought for Council deliberation even if no formal unresolved compliance issue exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (well-funded investigators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators currently awarded $2.0 million or more in total costs through certain NIH research mechanisms are subject to Special Council Review (SCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council will receive lists of affected PIs and applications; SCR is a threshold for additional consideration, not an automatic bar to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (foreign applications and international collaborations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applications and domestic or foreign primary applications that include foreign projects (foreign components) are subject to Special Council Review; foreign projects must be funded as primary awards, not sub-awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH requires submission to NOFOs that allow foreign applications or international components; Council will review such applications with additional scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (reinstatement of research aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for which the Division/Office is requesting to reinstate Specific Aims or research not recommended for support by the study section require Council discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to reinstate aims that were not recommended by study section trigger Council review of the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (restoration of budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for which the Division/Office is requesting to reinstate some or all of the budget not recommended by the study section require Council discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget restoration requests should be justified and are subject to Council scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (not discussed applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any 'Not discussed' applications a Division/Office proposes to award require Council discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards for applications not discussed in peer review require explicit Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (non-peer-reviewed applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain circumstances (e.g., type 4 MERIT awards), Council may perform both initial peer review and second-level review functions and must discuss non-peer-reviewed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-peer-reviewed award uses are limited and require Council deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special actions requiring Council discussion (deferred applications and appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications deferred from the previous Council (independent of review results) and Appeals (formerly called rebuttals) where applicants appeal peer review for flaws in the review process require Council consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred items and appeals are brought back for full Council review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting outcome codes and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting options include: Concurrence (concur with initial review recommendation), Other (an unusual action, optional), Deferred (if additional information is required or re-review needed), and Not Recommended by Council (non-concurrence with initial review). A Council may not change the outcome of initial peer review numeric scores or designation as competitive but not discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Other" is for unusual actions such as changes in recommended budget/duration and is optional at the IC's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in Special Council Review of well-funded investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: When making funding recommendations for PIs with >$2.0M in total costs, staff and Council members will consider: how innovative and distinct the pending project is from the PI’s other grants; the type of research (cost differences by field); the public health priority of the research; and how the absence of an award impacts other collaborative or translational research efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SCR is intended to steward public funds while allowing meritorious additional awards as warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in Special Council Review of foreign applications/international collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing foreign components, Council will consider: innovation/distinctness from PI's other grants; public health priority; whether the project presents special opportunities via unusual talent/resources/populations/environments abroad not readily available in the U.S.; whether the project is specifically relevant to the IC's mission and can significantly advance U.S. health sciences; and how absence of award impacts collaborative/translational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign components previously supported as subawards or consultants may continue to be supported under other activity codes unless NOFO specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited electronic review: eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff may request expedited electronic review for eligible applications; all Council members will be asked to participate, notified of applications, and will have secure access to summary statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited review may be designated for applications requiring immediate time-limited unique resources, administratively deferred or re-reviewed due to successful appeals, and RFAs; staff initiates expedited review requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early concurrence (en bloc early concurrence) process and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair will select two or more members to provide en bloc early concurrence on behalf of the full Council for a specified group of applications. The Executive Secretary will determine eligibility based on criteria similar to en bloc eligibility (overall impact score, not foreign, no unresolved human subject/animal/biohazard issues, no unresolved inclusion or appeal issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Council members receive lists of eligible applications; if any Council member requests full Council discussion by the response date, the application is removed from the early concurrence list. Concurrence by the majority of selected members is required; any single non-concurrence results in full Council consideration. A report of early concurrence recommendations is presented at each Council meeting; applications approved via early concurrence are eligible for funding once review is certified complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept review and actions on proposed FOAs/contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned research initiatives are presented as Concept Clearances describing objectives/rationale and scientific needs/opportunities; two or more Council members serve as reviewers ('discussants') of each concept and following discussion Council may: Approve with or without modifications, Disapprove, or Defer for further development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept Clearances are used to solicit Funding Opportunity Announcements or contract solicitations aligned with NCATS mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegations of authority for administrative funding adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council delegates authority to NCATS staff (program staff in consultation with Grants Management) to take administrative action without prior Council approval to award funds greater than the amount recommended by Council for research and training grants and cooperative agreements to support increased operational costs not anticipated at the time Council recommended approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative increases/extensions must be necessary for successful conduct, must not change basic goals/intent of the project, generally be no more than 25% of the current year's awarded direct costs, and a list of administrative supplements will be provided to Council for informational purposes. Examples include salary/fringe cost increases, increased F&A rates, equipment cost increases, minor modifications to take advantage of unanticipated opportunities, dissemination costs, orderly termination, bridge funding, and administrative correction of submission errors. All administrative supplements must be endorsed by the NCATS director and reported at the January meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements and extensions policy (duration and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with NIH policy, administrative supplements and extensions may be made to extend the period of support to ensure orderly termination or to support a project for a limited time pending a decision to continue or discontinue support (e.g., when support would terminate before completion of review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions should be as brief as possible and usually should not exceed one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee formation, authority, and quorum rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcommittees may be established by the executive secretary or other designated official; advice/recommendations of a subcommittee must be deliberated by the parent advisory committee; a subcommittee may not report directly to a federal official unless statutory authority exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A member of a standing subcommittee may serve as a voting member of another standing subcommittee but may not be counted toward determining a quorum. The quorum for a standing or ad hoc subcommittee is three.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional circumstances and documented deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of NCATS, after consultation with Council, may make exceptions to these guidelines based on programmatic considerations. Exceptions should be extremely rare to maintain consistent application across extramural divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions of an exceptional nature must be appropriately documented for the official record and reported to Council at its next scheduled meeting.
